concepts.title: Characteristics of Living Organisms
concepts.definition: Living organisms show features such as growth, movement, respiration, response to stimuli, reproduction, and excretion.
concepts.key_idea: All living things share certain life processes that distinguish them from non-living things.
question_patterns: What are the characteristics of living organisms?
How do living things grow?
What is respiration in living organisms?
Why is reproduction a characteristic of living things?
Give one example of a living thing responding to a stimulus.

solution_steps.explain: Decide whether the thing being studied is living or non-living.
Look for growth, respiration, movement, response to stimuli, and reproduction.
If it shows these life processes, it is a living organism.

worked_examples.question: List three characteristics of living organisms.
worked_examples.solution: Three characteristics are growth, respiration, and reproduction.
worked_examples.answer: Growth, respiration, reproduction.

worked_examples.question: How does a plant show that it is living?
worked_examples.solution: A plant grows, makes food, responds to light, and reproduces through seeds.
worked_examples.answer: A plant grows, makes food, responds to light, and reproduces.

exercises.question: What is respiration?
Give one example of a living thing responding to a stimulus.
Why is a stone not a living thing?

concepts.title: Classification of Living Organisms
concepts.definition: Classification is the arrangement of living organisms into groups based on shared features so they can be studied easily.
concepts.key_idea: Grouping organisms by similarities makes it easier to study the huge variety of life.
question_patterns: What is classification?
Why do we classify living organisms?
On what basis are organisms classified?
Give one example of classification in daily life.
How does classification help scientists?

solution_steps.explain: Look at the body features of the organisms being grouped.
Group organisms that share key features together.
State how the grouping makes study and identification easier.

worked_examples.question: Why do we classify living organisms?
worked_examples.solution: We classify so that the huge variety of life can be studied and identified easily.
worked_examples.answer: Classification makes it easy to study and identify organisms.

worked_examples.question: Give one example of classification in daily life.
worked_examples.solution: A library arranges books by subject so they can be found easily.
worked_examples.answer: A library arranges books by subject for easy finding.

exercises.question: What is classification?
Name one basis on which organisms are classified.
How does classification help scientists?

concepts.title: Plant and Animal Kingdoms
concepts.definition: Living organisms are broadly grouped into the plant kingdom and the animal kingdom based on how they get food and their body structure.
concepts.key_idea: Plants make their own food while animals depend on plants or other animals for food.
question_patterns: What are the two main kingdoms of living organisms?
How do plants differ from animals in getting food?
Why is a cow placed in the animal kingdom?
Give one feature of the plant kingdom.
How do animals get their food?

solution_steps.explain: Check whether the organism makes its own food or gets it from others.
Look for features like cell walls in plants or movement in animals.
Place the organism in the plant kingdom or animal kingdom based on these features.

worked_examples.question: What are the two main kingdoms of living organisms?
worked_examples.solution: The two main kingdoms are the plant kingdom and the animal kingdom.
worked_examples.answer: Plant kingdom and animal kingdom.

worked_examples.question: How do plants differ from animals in getting food?
worked_examples.solution: Plants make their own food using sunlight, while animals eat plants or other animals.
worked_examples.answer: Plants make food; animals eat plants or other animals.

exercises.question: Why is a mango tree in the plant kingdom?
Give one feature of the animal kingdom.
How do plants make their food?

concepts.title: Groups of Plants: Herbs, Shrubs, and Trees
concepts.definition: Plants are grouped by height and stem type into herbs (small soft stems), shrubs (medium woody stems), and trees (tall woody stems with branches).
concepts.key_idea: The height and type of stem help us group plants into herbs, shrubs, and trees.
question_patterns: What is a herb?
How is a shrub different from a tree?
Classify a mango plant as herb, shrub, or tree.
Give one example of a herb.
On what basis are plants grouped into herbs, shrubs, and trees?

solution_steps.explain: Look at how tall the plant is and whether its stem is soft or woody.
Small soft-stemmed plants are herbs, medium woody plants are shrubs, and tall woody plants are trees.
Check the grouping against a known example such as mint as a herb or mango as a tree.

worked_examples.question: Classify a mango plant as herb, shrub, or tree.
worked_examples.solution: A mango plant has a tall woody stem with branches, so it is a tree.
worked_examples.answer: Tree.

worked_examples.question: Give one example each of a herb, a shrub, and a tree.
worked_examples.solution: Mint is a herb, rose is a shrub, and mango is a tree.
worked_examples.answer: Herb: mint, shrub: rose, tree: mango.

worked_examples.question: How is a shrub different from a tree?
worked_examples.solution: A shrub is medium-sized with several woody stems, while a tree is tall with one main woody trunk.
worked_examples.answer: A shrub is medium with many stems; a tree is tall with one trunk.

exercises.question: What is a herb?
Classify a rose plant as herb, shrub, or tree.
Give one example of a tree.

concepts.title: Groups of Animals: Vertebrates and Invertebrates
concepts.definition: Animals are grouped by the presence of a backbone into vertebrates (with a backbone) and invertebrates (without a backbone).
concepts.key_idea: The backbone is a key feature used to divide animals into two large groups.
question_patterns: What is a vertebrate?
What is an invertebrate?
Classify an earthworm as vertebrate or invertebrate.
Give one example of a vertebrate.
On what basis are animals divided into vertebrates and invertebrates?

solution_steps.explain: Decide whether the animal has an internal backbone.
If it has a backbone it is a vertebrate; if not, it is an invertebrate.
Match the grouping to a known example such as a dog as a vertebrate or a worm as an invertebrate.

worked_examples.question: Classify an earthworm as vertebrate or invertebrate.
worked_examples.solution: An earthworm has no backbone, so it is an invertebrate.
worked_examples.answer: Invertebrate.

worked_examples.question: Give one example each of a vertebrate and an invertebrate.
worked_examples.solution: A frog is a vertebrate and a butterfly is an invertebrate.
worked_examples.answer: Vertebrate: frog, invertebrate: butterfly.

worked_examples.question: What is the main difference between vertebrates and invertebrates?
worked_examples.solution: Vertebrates have a backbone while invertebrates do not.
worked_examples.answer: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not.

exercises.question: What is a vertebrate?
Classify a fish as vertebrate or invertebrate.
Give one example of an invertebrate.

concepts.title: Habitats and Adaptations
concepts.definition: A habitat is the natural place where an organism lives, and an adaptation is a feature that helps it survive there.
concepts.key_idea: Organisms have special features that help them live in their habitats.
question_patterns: What is a habitat?
What is an adaptation?
Give one example of an adaptation in a desert animal.
How does a fish adapt to water?
Why do organisms need adaptations?

solution_steps.explain: Determine where the organism lives, such as desert, forest, or water.
Find a body feature or behaviour that helps it survive there.
Show how the adaptation suits the conditions of the habitat.

worked_examples.question: Give one example of an adaptation in a desert animal.
worked_examples.solution: A camel stores fat in its hump and can go long without water, helping it survive in the desert.
worked_examples.answer: A camel's hump stores fat and helps it survive without water.

worked_examples.question: How does a fish adapt to water?
worked_examples.solution: A fish has gills to breathe underwater and fins to swim.
worked_examples.answer: Gills to breathe and fins to swim.

exercises.question: What is a habitat?
Give one example of an adaptation in a plant.
Why do organisms need adaptations?

concepts.title: Adaptations to Different Habitats
concepts.definition: Different habitats such as deserts, mountains, forests, and water need different adaptations like storing water, thick fur, or streamlined bodies.
concepts.key_idea: Adaptations match the conditions of the habitat where an organism lives.
question_patterns: How do desert plants adapt to less water?
Give one adaptation of a mountain animal.
How does a polar bear survive in the cold?
Why do aquatic animals have streamlined bodies?
Compare adaptations in desert and water habitats.

solution_steps.explain: Decide the kind of habitat, such as desert, mountain, or water.
Note the main challenges like heat, cold, or low water.
Find the features that help the organism survive those conditions.

worked_examples.question: How do desert plants adapt to less water?
worked_examples.solution: Desert plants like cactus have spines and thick stems to store water and reduce loss.
worked_examples.answer: Cactus has spines and thick stems to store water.

worked_examples.question: Give one adaptation of a mountain animal.
worked_examples.solution: A snow leopard has thick fur to keep warm in the cold mountains.
worked_examples.answer: Thick fur keeps a snow leopard warm.

worked_examples.question: Why do aquatic animals have streamlined bodies?
worked_examples.solution: A streamlined body reduces water resistance so they can swim easily.
worked_examples.answer: Streamlined bodies reduce water resistance for easy swimming.

exercises.question: How does a polar bear survive in the cold?
Give one adaptation of a desert animal.
Why do mountain trees have cone shapes?

concepts.title: Biodiversity
concepts.definition: Biodiversity is the variety of living organisms found in a particular area, including plants, animals, and microorganisms.
concepts.key_idea: The huge variety of life on Earth is called biodiversity.
question_patterns: What is biodiversity?
Why is biodiversity important?
Give one example of biodiversity in a forest.
How does biodiversity help humans?
Why should we protect biodiversity?

solution_steps.explain: Choose the place whose variety of life you want to study.
List the different kinds of plants, animals, and microorganisms there.
Describe how this variety keeps the area healthy and useful.

worked_examples.question: What is biodiversity?
worked_examples.solution: Biodiversity is the variety of living organisms in a particular area.
worked_examples.answer: The variety of living organisms in an area.

worked_examples.question: Give one example of biodiversity in a forest.
worked_examples.solution: A forest has trees, birds, insects, and deer living together, showing high biodiversity.
worked_examples.answer: A forest has trees, birds, insects, and deer together.

worked_examples.question: Why is biodiversity important?
worked_examples.solution: Biodiversity keeps ecosystems balanced and provides food, medicine, and clean air.
worked_examples.answer: It keeps ecosystems balanced and provides food, medicine, and clean air.

exercises.question: Why should we protect biodiversity?
Give one example of biodiversity near your home.
How does biodiversity help humans?

concepts.title: Counting Groups of Organisms
concepts.definition: We can count how many organisms belong to each group in a habitat to compare the diversity of groups.
concepts.formula: total = sum of organisms in each group
concepts.key_idea: Adding the counts of each group gives the total number of organisms in a sample.
question_patterns: a habitat has {count1} herbs, {count2} shrubs and {count3} trees -- how many plants are there in total?
count the total organisms if there are {count1} vertebrates and {count2} invertebrates.
how many animals are there if {count1} are vertebrates and {count2} are invertebrates?
find the total number of plants given {count1} herbs and {count2} trees.
if a sample has {count1} herbs, {count2} shrubs and {count3} trees, what is the total?

solution_steps.action: List the counts of each group
solution_steps.explain: Write down how many organisms are in each group.
add the counts of all the groups, e.g. 5 + 3 + 2 = 10 plants
Check that the total equals the sum of the individual group counts.

worked_examples.question: A habitat has 5 herbs, 3 shrubs, and 2 trees. How many plants are there in total?
worked_examples.solution: Add the counts: 5 + 3 + 2 = 10.
worked_examples.answer: 10 plants.

worked_examples.question: Count the total animals if there are 4 vertebrates and 6 invertebrates.
worked_examples.solution: Add the counts: 4 + 6 = 10.
worked_examples.answer: 10 animals.

worked_examples.question: If a sample has 2 herbs, 4 shrubs, and 3 trees, what is the total number of plants?
worked_examples.solution: Add the counts: 2 + 4 + 3 = 9.
worked_examples.answer: 9 plants.

exercises.question: A habitat has 6 herbs and 4 trees. Find the total number of plants.
Count the total animals if there are 3 vertebrates and 8 invertebrates.
If there are 5 herbs, 2 shrubs, and 1 tree, what is the total?
